items.title: [ArchDaily] Tiny House Razzi / Stanaćev Granados
items.content_html: This small cabin, with just a 35 m² footprint plus an additional 10 square meters of loft space on its upper level, was designed to be a prototype for a tiny home. It was commissioned to us by a French contractor established in Chile, with whom we collaborated to develop this prototype of an architectural solution implementing a prefabricated construction system he had conceived.

items.title: [ArchDaily] House Up in the Clouds / Hennessey Architecture
items.content_html: Located in the foggy and windy Diamond Heights neighborhood of San Francisco, this fully renovated three-story 1962 Eichler residence includes a fourth level addition that serves to make the home more functional for a growing young family. This upper level addition contains a family room, bathroom, and roof deck, but there was a fundamental issue with the location of this new family room area; it is located two levels above the living/dining/kitchen level of the home, thereby risking not being used on a day-to-day basis.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Lion Green Road / Mary Duggan Architects
items.content_html: Lion Green Road is a residential-led scheme comprising five buildings containing 157 dwellings. The project sits within a verdant landscape in Coulsdon, London Borough of Croydon, within a geographical chalk basin. The wider context is varied typologically, including an extensive low-rise green belt development to the south on higher ground by Barratt Homes, delivering 667 homes alongside retained extensive lush open land. A traditional low-rise suburban grain populates the northern side of the site, also ascending toward Crystal Palace.

items.title: [ArchDaily] House in Yakami / enter-archi
items.content_html: House in Yakami explores how architecture can respond to the landscape through bodily experience, rather than simply consuming its beauty as a view. The site is located in Yakami, Onan Town, Shimane Prefecture, surrounded by the Chugoku Mountains.

items.title: [ArchDaily] The House of Courtyards / Studio VDGA
items.content_html: Set in the city of gold, Dubai, this villa was one of the most challenging projects considering the diverse architectural languages that the city follows. Be it the towering skyscrapers, extremely modern boxed structures, or ornate villas, the city sees a lot in spatial expression. Various themes were scrapped, and many ideas were renegotiated till we found a form that very closely mirrors desert architecture.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Konya Square Houses and Bicycle Museum Extension / Yalin Architectural Design
items.content_html: Konya Square Houses consists of 13 reinforced-concrete buildings constructed in 2005, drawing on the traditional Konya houses and neighborhood fabric that existed on the site until 1955. Over the years, the complex accommodated various non-governmental organizations and municipal departments.

items.title: [ArchDaily] DamDam House / Studio SMA + Ground Architects
items.content_html: DamDam is a compact house for a couple, their twins, and two cats, designed with solid exterior walls to ensure privacy on a small site surrounded by taller buildings. Working within the constraints of the parking layout, the functions of each floor were carefully separated, and the circulation was precisely planned to maximize the usability of the interior spaces.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Virtual Studio at the Cidade das TIC, A Coruña Arms Factory / Diaz y Diaz Architects
items.content_html: In the former Weapons Factory of A Coruña, the Virtual Studio translates an essential duality into architecture: a hermetic box designed to create digital worlds versus an open volume that dialogues with the landscape and the industrial memory of the site.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Alonakia House / React Architects
items.content_html: Situated on a steep west-facing slope in Antiparos, the house overlooks the open Aegean and the long horizon of the setting sun. Its design begins with the condition of the site: a rugged terrain in which building is inseparable from the act of shaping the ground. Instead of introducing a singular object onto the hillside, the project is conceived as a continuation of the existing topography, translating the characteristics of the Cycladic landscape into a contemporary dwelling.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Rotiers - Renovation of 46 housing units in Brussels  / MULTIPLE Architecture & Urbanism
items.content_html: The Rotiers project aims to give a renewed architectural identity to a 1960s social housing building while preserving the qualities of its setting. Located at the edge of the Sonian Forest and surrounded by mature trees, the building is renovated in close relation to its landscape. The intervention addresses several scales, from the building's integration into the neighborhood to the everyday experience of residents and neighbors, with particular attention to the dwellings, shared outdoor spaces, and entrances.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Villa Moderne: In Search of Hong Kong Modern Homes
items.content_html:
Recreating the modern villas that shaped Hong Kong from the 1930s to the 1980s, this book offers a glimpse into the architecture and lifestyles of high society, tracing how these homes helped shape the city’s neighbourhoods and urban history.

Hong Kong’s modern villas reveal a side of the city rarely seen in its skyline. From the 1930s onwards, they appeared on hillsides, beside coastal roads and in newly planned suburbs, reflecting changing ideas of what a modern home could be.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Include Enable Connect
items.content_html:
Include Enable Connect captures hcma's evolving framework for maximizing social impact through design.
It represents a body of work developed by hcma over many years, and draws on the thinking and experience of our leadership group and project teams, conversations with collaborators and communities, and a wide field of academic research.
Written for architects, project teams, and building operators, it offers a structured way to move from intention to action so we can think more clearly about the social role of the places we create.
At its heart, it's about using design as a tool to support connection, wellbeing, and lasting civic life.

items.title: [ArchDaily] From Coastal Reclamation to Data Centers: How India's Architecture Grows Around Water
items.content_html: Architecture has treated water either as a backdrop or a problem: a view to be framed, a hazard to be drained, or a utility to be connected. In contemporary India, a more consequential relationship takes shape. Water remains a shared ecological resource, yet the land and infrastructure around it are increasingly financed and defended as economic assets. Coastlines are extended to carry traffic and lake edges become lucrative development zones. The decision to do so passes through multiple institutions with different vocabularies, thereby challenging who determines how water and its surroundings are used, and who faces the consequences.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Modern Architecture in Bahia: Climate and Culture in the Work of Assis Reis
items.content_html: Last October 24th marked the centenary of the birth of Brazilian architect Francisco de Assis Couto Reis (1926–2011), who lived and built most of his work in the city of Salvador, Bahia. Assis Reis, as he was better known, had a career shaped not only by the buildings he designed but also by his urban renewal proposals, his design for the Brazilian Pavilion at the World Expo in Osaka, Japan (unbuilt), and the Scale Model of the City of Salvador, landmarked in 2020. His vast and diverse body of work belongs to a specific moment of modern expression in Brazil, when architects of this "second generation" were particularly concerned with adapting to local climatic, geographical, and cultural conditions.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Beyond Affordable Housing: Integrating Civic Infrastructure in US Mixed-Use Developments
items.content_html: For much of the twentieth century, affordable housing in the United States was conceived as a distinct residential category, shaped by financing structures and development practices that separated housing for lower-income residents from the broader civic and commercial functions of the city. Federal housing legislation and subsequent urban renewal policies contributed to the construction of large residential developments that were frequently financed and managed independently of surrounding urban infrastructure. The consequences of this approach, including concentrated poverty, deteriorating buildings, unequal access to services, and the eventual demolition of prominent public housing projects, are extensively documented.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Umodzi Epicentre Community Center / Kamuna Design Studio
items.content_html: 'Mutu umodzi susenza denga' — one head cannot carry a roof. The Chichewa proverb gives Umodzi its name, and describes how it was made. In Vubwi District, on the border of Malawi and Mozambique, a community hand molded bricks, raised walls and carried the roofs of a place that now supports education, training and care for more than 26,000 people in 126 villages.
